The study was conducted to predict the flow field within the NASA Lewis Transonic Turbine Blade Cascade Facility, which is used to evaluate rocket propulsion turbines.
A pitchwise non-uniform total pressure distribution was observed at the blade row leading edge plane.
The PARC code, a general purpose, three-dimensional, Navier-Stokes code with multi-block solution capability, was used for the computational analysis.
The computational analysis of the original geometry showed total pressure loss regions consistent in strength and location to experimental measurements.
The cause of the flow non-uniformity was a pair of vortices that originated from an embedded bellmouth inlet in the original geometry.
A redesigned inlet section that eliminated the embedded bellmouth by bridging the region between it and the upstream wall was analyzed computationally.
The analysis of the redesigned inlet section indicated that eliminating the embedded bellmouth eliminated the troublesome pair of vortices, resulting in a flow with much greater pitchwise uniformity.

A computational approach was chosen over an experimental approach because physical accessibility to the inlet section was limited, and a computational approach allows for examining design changes cheaper and more quickly.
